note: The CEO's own goal, carried by the Chief of Staff seat. There is no executive pillar and the dashboard iterates hq/data/pillars.json, so this file is read by the dashboard's side panel instead: server.waiting_block() takes the statement and the target from here and puts them beside the live reading, and server.record_queue_night() writes that reading to hq/data/history/queue.jsonl once each evening. Both readings it is measured on, queue_state / waiting_on_you and queue_state / oldest_waiting_days, count through server.waiting_on_you(), which is also what the dashboard's own decision and work counts are taken from.

verdict_template.unassured: Nothing is failing; we are still building checks for {unassured} of the {total} areas, and the plans for those are written.

goals.statement_short: At the end of every day, the list of things waiting on Daniel is empty.
goals.why_it_matters: Every other seat in the studio can be run in parallel. Daniel cannot. Whatever waits on him is the one queue that sets the pace of the whole company, and while it has anything in it he is answering instead of building. In his words: it "represents the bottleneck of what I can contribute, and I obviously cannot parallelize myself." Until it is burned to zero he cannot make net-new contributions to the game, which is what his time is for.

measure.label: decision cards prepped for him plus finished work awaiting his verdict, counted at the end of the day

path_to_green.narrative: Two things keep the count above zero: work that never needed him arrives anyway, and every answer he gives files new cards that come straight back to him. The plan in docs/QUEUE_TO_ZERO.md closes both — finished, verified, revertable work lands on its own and is reported, not judged; a follow-up may reach him only when it is a genuine question with a recommendation attached — and then shows him each remaining item in a form that costs him under a minute to answer.

action.label: Put it on the Chief of Staff's list
action.title: Let verified, revertable work land without a verdict from Daniel
action.ask: Build the arrival policy in docs/QUEUE_TO_ZERO.md: a finished tier-0 or tier-1 card whose suites are green on a clean worktree, whose checker has no open finding and whose text passes the writing check is landed and reported in a digest, never placed in his queue. A card that fails goes back to its owner, not to him.
action.first_action: Read docs/QUEUE_TO_ZERO.md, then change hq/drain.py's write_back so a card meeting the landing bar goes to a 'landed' state with a revert control, and hq/work.py's tier-0 worker does the same for a reading whose follow-ups are all revertable.
